Flat even diagram lighting, a quiet nostalgic warmth. Compose the card as ONE single calm everyday scene, readable like a still from a silent film: the moment is carried entirely by the people, their faces and gestures, the objects they hold and the setting. Show clearly who turns to whom, where, and the thing the moment is about. Only the gestures the staging names; no extra handshake, wave, pointing finger or thumb-up. Keep the subject large and dominant in the foreground, floating cleanly on the cream paper on a simple background. The main picture alone makes this card's word obvious at a glance: the subject is the largest and most central element, shown in its most recognisable form and in the action that defines it, and the insets only add supporting detail. Any people who appear are ordinary Lithuanian civilians in plain everyday clothes of 1981, dressed for the setting and the weather: shirts, cardigans, simple dresses and headscarves indoors and on the street; coats, caps and hats outdoors in cold weather. Every person in a group is a different individual, with a distinct face, age, build, hair and clothing colour. This is a spoken moment. The person who speaks and the person spoken to look at each other, eyes on each other's face, heads turned toward one another; where the staging has the speaker look or point at a thing (a clock, a shelf, the rain), the listener looks at the speaker or at that thing. Nobody in the picture looks at the viewer or toward the camera; no face is turned to the front with eyes past the viewer's shoulder. Bystanders look at their own task or at the speakers. Only include people the subject or scene actually calls for; do not add an extra standing figure that is not needed. Any arrow or callout, drawn in solid black ink, points only at the subject the card teaches or at the direction of its motion. Render NO text, NO lettering, NO numbers, NO words, NO labels and NO captions anywhere in the image — no leader-line labels, no writing in any panel, on any flag, sign, or object, and none in the header or footer bands. Frame the card with a plain solid deep, dark brick-red horizontal band across the very top and another across the very bottom, plus a thin band of the same dark red around the whole card. When the staging names a right or left hand, that hand and no other performs the action, drawn on the correct side of the body as the viewer sees it. Flat even diagram lighting, a quiet nostalgic warmth. People are ordinary Lithuanians of 1981, anonymous types with correct natural proportions, each person a different individual: fair skin, ash-blond to light-brown hair, grey or blue-grey eyes, broad-cheeked oval faces, straight noses, calm closed mouths, austere and plainly handsome. Men side-parted or cropped, some moustached, working men in flat caps; women blond or light-brown-haired, the younger ones lean, with hair mostly straight, now and then faintly waved or neatly styled; older women in the usual range of everyday styles, plain, pinned back or set, occasionally curled, or under a cotton headscarf; clothes plain and loosely cut, in brown, olive, dusty blue, grey and dull red, chosen for the setting and occasion. Heads turn at varied natural angles: in a group most look at their task or at each other and one or two face the viewer, eyes just past the viewer's shoulder; of two main figures only one faces the viewer; a lone figure stands near-frontal, face turned only a little. Subject: the everyday moment that calls for the question word 'where'. Staging: a man in a hallway patting his coat pockets and looking round the room, keys missing, a hook on the wall empty; no bubble, no lettering. The detail that makes this moment unmistakable, clearly visible at small size: searching posture, empty hook. Compose the card as ONE single calm everyday scene, readable like a still from a silent film: the moment is carried entirely by the people, their faces and gestures, the objects they hold and the setting. Show clearly who turns to whom, where, and the thing the moment is about. Only the gestures the staging names; no extra handshake, wave, pointing finger or thumb-up. Keep the subject large and dominant in the foreground, floating cleanly on the cream paper on a simple background. The main picture alone makes this card's word obvious at a glance: the subject is the largest and most central element, shown in its most recognisable form and in the action that defines it, and the insets only add supporting detail. Any people who appear are ordinary Lithuanian civilians in plain everyday clothes of 1981, dressed for the setting and the weather: shirts, cardigans, simple dresses and headscarves indoors and on the street; coats, caps and hats outdoors in cold weather. Every person in a group is a different individual, with a distinct face, age, build, hair and clothing colour. Of two main figures, one faces the viewer with eyes resting just past the viewer's shoulder and the other looks at the task, at the first figure, or into the scene. Only include people the subject or scene actually calls for; do not add an extra standing figure that is not needed. Every object, tool and fixture is complete, attached and in working order: hanging things hang from a proper rack or hook, doorways and corridors stay clear and passable, furniture rests on the floor against a wall, tools are held in a usable grip, machines and vehicles are whole and correctly scaled to the people, and a resting animal is visibly alive and at ease, eyes closed and body relaxed. Every surface is dead-matte, as absorbent offset paper prints it: skin, hair, fabric, leather, metal, glass, water and polished wood carry flat ink tone and one soft shadow tone only. Any arrow or callout, drawn in solid black ink, points only at the subject the card teaches or at the direction of its motion. Render NO text, NO lettering, NO numbers, NO words, NO labels and NO captions anywhere in the image — no leader-line labels, no writing in any panel, on any flag, sign, or object, and none in the header or footer bands. Any area that would normally hold text must be left completely blank. No speech bubbles, thought bubbles or floating symbols of any kind; meaning is carried by people, gestures, objects and setting. Frame the card with a plain solid deep, dark brick-red horizontal band across the very top and another across the very bottom, plus a thin band of the same dark red around the whole card. These bands are blank design elements and must contain no text whatsoever. Keep ALL illustration content — every figure, object, and inset panel — fully inside the inner frame; nothing may overlap, touch, or extend across the red header or footer bands. If any national emblem is shown at all, use ONLY a small Lithuanian tricolor flag (a horizontal yellow band on top, green in the middle, red on the bottom), placed small and only where it fits naturally. Do NOT include coats of arms, the Vytis knight, the Columns of Gediminas, or any other heraldic emblem or badge. Do not put a flag on every card — many cards need no emblem at all. Render every human hand with clean natural anatomy and exactly five fingers. Every arm and hand belongs to one body and is drawn joined to that body's shoulder: no hand floats, no arm crosses from one person onto another, and when two people stand close each one's arms stay on their own side. When the staging names a right or left hand, that hand and no other performs the action, drawn on the correct side of the body as the viewer sees it. An object a person is said to carry, hold or hand over is visibly in that person's grip, fingers closed round the handle or the object, its weight on that hand. People stand beside, behind or in front of furniture, counters, rails and vehicles, never inside or merged with them: a person behind a counter is cut off by its top edge and nothing else; a seated person sits on the seat. Faces are whole and each face is its own. Finish: dead-matte offset print on light aged cream paper with a faint yellow cast, brush-ink outlines, soft shading, correct proportions, flat tone on skin, hair, cloth and metal. One or two faces toward the viewer, eyes just past the shoulder; of two main figures only one. Every inset a clearly different moment, all in the same ruled frame. Diagram arrows and callouts in solid black ink.
